title: Error Analysis and Model Interpretation knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Investigating incorrect predictions” in this lesson?
options: This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Segment-wise analysis”, what should a learner verify?
options: Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
verify class/target shapes, threshold choices, split independence, and that model selection did not repeatedly use test results.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
questions.answer_key: verify class/target shapes, threshold choices, split independence, and that model selection did not repeatedly use test results.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: verify class/target shapes, threshold choices, split independence, and that model selection did not repeatedly use test results.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Feature and input sensitivity”?
options: Do not use the test split to tune a model and then present the same score as an unbiased final test.
Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
questions.answer_key: Do not use the test split to tune a model and then present the same score as an unbiased final test.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not use the test split to tune a model and then present the same score as an unbiased final test.
